title: X4 · Kavya’s question: why are writes so fast?
description: A new teammate spots something odd on the dashboard. Answer her on the whiteboard by drawing what happens to each write, now and later.

problemStatement.overview:
**#orders-eng, Monday 10:14**

> **Kavya** (joined last week): Dumb question. orders-db p99 write latency is a flat **2 ms**, all day. But the disk graph has **huge write bursts every few minutes** and **constant background reads**. If the disk is that busy, why don’t writes slow down?

> **Neha**: Not dumb at all. Whoever’s free, grab the whiteboard and walk her through it.

You’re free. Draw the life of one write, `PUT order:88213 → status=paid`, so Kavya can see **which part is the 2 ms** and **which parts are the bursts and the background reads**.
problemStatement.yourTask: Place six cards so Kavya can see the fast part and the background part of every write.
yourTaskSteps: Each block’s prompt says whether it’s the 2 ms part or the background part.
Submit when you think Kavya would get it.
hints: The 2 ms is one sequential append plus a memory insert.
The bursts are big files being written. The background reads are files being merged.
problemStatement.moat: Classic. Same chain as ds-01. Unlocks X5.

platformSpec.kicker: Experiment X4 · Teammate question · Unlocks X5
platformSpec.passMessage: Kavya: “Oh. The 2 ms is just the log append and the memtable. The bursts are flushes and the reads are compaction. Got it.” X5 is now unlocked.

pieces.title: Append to the WAL and fsync
pieces.blurb: One small sequential write at the end of a file. Fast.

pieces.title: Insert into the memtable, reply OK
pieces.blurb: A memory insert into a sorted tree. Microseconds.

pieces.title: Freeze the full memtable, start a new one
pieces.blurb: Every 64 MB. New writes go straight to the new memtable, so nobody waits.

pieces.title: Flush 64 MB to a new SSTable
pieces.blurb: One big sequential write. This is a burst on Kavya’s graph.

pieces.title: Write a Bloom filter and index
pieces.blurb: Small extra file next to the SSTable for faster reads.

pieces.title: Delete the WAL segment
pieces.blurb: Its records are all in the SSTable now.

pieces.title: Compaction reads and merges SSTables
pieces.blurb: Reads several files and writes merged ones. These are the constant background reads.

pieces.title: Overwrite the order’s page on disk
pieces.blurb: A random write to wherever the old value lives.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: That’s a B-tree. If LSM did this, writes would be slow random I/O.

pieces.title: Split the full page
pieces.blurb: Rebalance the tree when a page overflows.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: B-tree behaviour. No pages in an LSM tree.

pieces.title: Reply OK first, write the log later
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Faster, but a crash loses acknowledged orders.

pieces.title: Write an SSTable for every PUT
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Thousands of tiny files a second. Writes and reads would both crawl.

pieces.title: Pause writes during compaction
pieces.trapIfPlaced: If that happened, Kavya would see latency spikes, not a flat 2 ms.
